action: Maersk customers and partners: watch for company updates on what data was involved, be alert to invoices or shipping messages that look unusual, and verify any payment-detail change by phone.
exec: Maersk disclosed data theft from a system inherited through an acquisition; it says findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed.
plain: Shipping company Maersk confirmed that an intruder took data from systems of a company it acquired. A criminal group called WhiteArmor demands $5 million and says it will publish about 100GB of data.
summary: Maersk said an intruder breached a legacy system inherited through an earlier acquisition and stole data; its advisory says the incident is isolated to a local system and findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed. The WhiteArmor group claimed the attack and says it holds about 100GB (unverified), threatening to publish it unless paid $5 million.
title: Maersk confirms data theft; WhiteArmor demands $5 million

validation.note: BleepingComputer and Computing (read) both relay Maersk's customer advisory of 11 Nov. Maersk has not named the acquired company or confirmed WhiteArmor. Computing reports a WhiteArmor deadline of 7 December.

review.note: Checked against BleepingComputer and Computing: 11 Nov advisory, 100GB, 5M claim match. Exec stated no sensitive data disclosed flatly and an unsourced way-in claim; now Maersk's 'findings so far strongly suggest' wording.
